minutes.headline: Water commissioners favored a separate bill line for the new water main loan and voted to buy more voting clickers.
minutes.summary: The board heard the annual audit from the district's auditor, who called the district financially well positioned. After approving prior minutes it began budget talks: legal fees, health insurance, and how to show the new water main loan separately from operating costs. It also moved to buy more voting clickers, and discussed state loan funding, pilot studies, the new bylaws and a hydrant access fix.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the regular meeting and the special meeting of January 10th.
Spend an amount heard as $771 to buy additional voting remotes (clickers), paid from the maintenance budget.

budget_items.what_was_said: The auditor reported water revenues up year over year while other operating revenue such as connection fees fell, leaving total revenue up modestly.

budget_items.topic: Audit: utilities and operating expense increases
budget_items.what_was_said: Utilities, heating, group insurance and professional fees rose; subcontracting fell. Professional fees were affected by the 2022 audit fee landing in this year.
Testing costs rose due to a one-time pump test on a well and a Hickory Hills pilot study, expected to drop next year.

budget_items.topic: Audit: total operating expenses and change in net position
budget_items.what_was_said: Total operating expenses rose; net position change was positive, and one-time costs would have made it higher.
Rental income fell after a lease ended; state contract assistance on loans varies year to year and is not controllable by the district.
Cash rose and receivables fell; pension and retiree benefit liabilities rose but are not controlled by the district.
Another loan was paid off, leaving two big loans; outstanding debt and interest payments dropped.
Legal spending year to date was first misstated and then corrected after a surplus-funded item was removed; board leaned toward raising the legal line from the current level.
The treasurer used the high projected increase for health insurance; the town's rates reportedly came in lower on average.
Maintenance and chemical lines were about half spent seven months in, with winter the low-usage quarter; utilities and fuel were down.

budget_items.topic: Water main replacement loan and bill line
budget_items.what_was_said: A new loan for the water main project would be repaid through a separate fixed line on customer bills starting July 1, kept out of the operating budget.
The Hickory Hills loan was approved with a zero-interest rate and anticipated principal forgiveness, not guaranteed.
The litigation team asked questions about the well's pumping capacity; the superintendent pushed a higher figure to support recovery.
The town's draft agreement pays grants half within 30 days of signing and half by reimbursement, with monthly reports.
Board discussed buying extra keypads for large meetings, sharing with the town; a quote for more units was mentioned, with possible negotiation.

decisions.decision: Board leaned toward raising the legal fees budget line to somewhere between the two figures discussed; the treasurer will fold it into the draft.
Treasurer to prepare a format showing the water main loan separately, and the board aims to finalize the budget at the next meeting.
Board will have legal counsel review the new bylaws for conflicts with state law, while the clerk signs and stamps them as voted.
